reason: E3 states that HEAs have low, almost temperature-independent lattice thermal conductivity due to force-constant disorder, supporting the first two premises. E2 shows oxygen contamination is a major issue in HfNbTaTiZr fabrication, supporting the fourth premise. However, no cited evidence supports the claim that electronic conductivity increases markedly at high temperatures in this specific alloy, nor the quantitative 25–30% improvement, as E1 concerns Ni-based alloys and E3 does not provide temperature-dependent electronic transport data for HfNbTaTiZr.
premises: Intrinsic force-constant disorder from multicomponent mixing dominates phonon scattering in defect-free HfNbTaTiZr
Lattice thermal conductivity is nearly temperature-independent at low temperatures in this alloy
Electronic thermal conductivity increases markedly at elevated temperatures due to disordered electronic structure
Oxygen contamination significantly reduces total thermal conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr
Decoupling lattice and electronic transport yields 25–30% higher total conductivity than oxygen-contaminated samples
